title: How to Know If Your Air Ducts Need Cleaning
h1: How Do You Know If Your Air Ducts Need Cleaning?
description: Dust blowing from vents, musty odors or signs of pests can mean your ducts need cleaning. Learn the signs to look for and what a proper cleaning involves.
quick_answer: Your ducts likely need cleaning if you see dust or debris blowing from vents, find visible buildup inside the registers, notice musty smells, or have had rodents, a remodel or smoke get into the system. Not every home needs it on a set schedule. An inspection tells you whether cleaning will actually help.
body:
Duct cleaning isn't something every home needs every year. But when ducts do get dirty, that dust and debris rides along with every cycle of the heat or AC and settles all over your house. Here's how to tell whether yours need attention.

What are the signs your air ducts need cleaning?

  • Dust puffs out of vents when the system starts
  • Visible buildup on supply registers or inside the duct when you pull a vent cover
  • Dust returns quickly after you clean, even with a fresh filter
  • Musty or stale smells when the system runs
  • Signs of pests such as droppings, nesting material or scratching sounds in the ducts
  • Recent remodeling that put drywall dust or sawdust into the system
  • Smoke exposure from a nearby wildfire or a house fire
  • Allergy symptoms that ease when you leave home

One sign on its own isn't proof. A dusty house can come from many things. Two or three together, especially visible debris in the ducts, is a strong reason to get them checked.

How can you check your ducts yourself?

  1. Turn the system off.
  2. Unscrew a supply register in a main room and one return grille.
  3. Shine a flashlight inside and take a phone picture as far in as you can reach.
  4. Look for thick dust, debris, pet hair, droppings or dark growth.
  5. Check the filter slot and the area around the blower if you can see it.

A light film of dust is normal. Clumps, layers you can write your name in, or anything that looks like mold or droppings is not.

What makes ducts get dirty faster?

Several things are common in our area. Ducts run through attics in many San Diego and Orange County homes, and loose connections there can pull in insulation dust and attic debris. Older tract homes often have original duct systems with years of buildup. Pets, construction, smoke events and filters that don't fit snugly all add to the load.

Return ducts are a big part of this. The return side pulls air back to the system, so any gap in a return duct running through the attic or garage sucks in whatever is around it. Garage returns can even pull in car exhaust and fumes from stored chemicals. Sealing those leaks keeps the system pulling air only from inside the living space.

Ducts that leak also pull in dirt from where they run. If cleaning keeps getting needed, the ducts may need sealing or repair too.

What does a professional duct cleaning include?

A thorough cleaning covers the whole system, not just the vents you can see:

  • Putting the ductwork under negative pressure with a powerful vacuum so debris is pulled out rather than blown into the house
  • Agitating each supply and return run with brushes or air whips
  • Cleaning registers, grilles and the return plenum
  • Checking the blower and coil, since a clean duct attached to a dirty blower won't stay clean
  • Sanitizing when there's been mold, pests or smoke

Our air duct cleaning service follows that full process and includes a look at the condition of the ductwork, so you'll know if anything needs sealing or repair.

What should you avoid?

Be cautious of anyone who wants to spray chemicals or coatings into your ducts as a first step, or who offers a whole-house cleaning that only takes an hour. A real cleaning reaches the full length of each run, and treatments should only be used when there's a specific reason, like confirmed mold. Ask what the process includes before work starts.

How often should air ducts be cleaned?

There's no single schedule that fits every home. Many homes go several years between cleanings without issues. Homes with pets, allergies, smoke exposure or attic ducts that leak may need it sooner. The best approach is to clean when an inspection shows buildup, rather than on a fixed calendar.

Between cleanings, change your filter on schedule and make sure it fits the slot with no gaps around the edges. That one habit keeps more dust out of your ducts than anything else.
faqs: Is air duct cleaning worth it?

It's worth it when there's real buildup, pests, mold or smoke in the system. If your ducts are clean on inspection, cleaning won't change much, and changing filters regularly is the better use of your money.
How long does air duct cleaning take?
Most homes take a few hours, depending on the number of vents, the size of the house and how dirty the system is. Homes with attic ductwork or heavy buildup can take longer.
Can I clean my air ducts myself?
You can vacuum registers and the first few inches of duct. Cleaning the full length of each run takes specialized vacuum and agitation equipment that most homeowners don't have.
Will duct cleaning help with allergies?
It can help when the ducts are holding dust, pet dander or pollen that keeps getting blown around. Pair it with a good filter and regular cleaning in the house for the best results.
